podcast.body: The Eagles released their cover of this song in 1978. Don Henley, who grew up hearing the original by blues legend Charles Brown in Texas, suggested it to the band, and Glenn Frey believed a bluesy track would be perfect for Henley's vocals. Henley's rendition stays true to the song's blues roots, offering a melancholy but bluesy tone. This single marked the first Eagles release featuring new bassist Timothy B. Schmidt, who replaced Randy Meisner. It reached number 18 on the Billboard charts and, at last check, was number 25 on the Billboard Holiday 100, serving to satisfy their record label while they worked on their next studio album. "Henley stays true to the blues roots of this song with his cover of Please Come Home for Christmas."
